### What the **`triangulation_metrics`** function does | Item | Description | |------|-------------| | **Purpose** | Pulls a list of *products* and *branches* that have had at least one “triangulation” run in the most recent 90 days (or a custom window you specify). | | **Return format** | A JSON array where each element represents a single triangulation run. Each object contains:
• `product_id` – the unique ID of the product.
• `branch_id` – the unique ID of the branch.
• `run_date` – ISO‑8601 timestamp of when the run finished.
• `metrics` – a nested object holding key performance indicators such as `accuracy`, `coverage`, `runtime_seconds`, etc. | | **Typical use‑case** | • Auditing recent triangulation activity.
• Feeding downstream dashboards that track run frequency per product/branch.
• Triggering alerts if a product has no runs in the past 30 days. | --- ### How to call it ```python from functions import requests_get response = requests_get( url="https://api.example.com/triangulation_metrics", headers={ "Accept": "application/json" }, params={ "days": 60, # optional – override the default 90‑day window "end_date": "2026-06-28" # optional – set a fixed cut‑off date }, cookies={ "session_id": "abc123", "auth_token": "Bearer xyz789" } ) data = response.json() # list of run objects ``` #### Parameters | Parameter | Type | Default | Notes | |-----------|------|---------|-------| | `days` | int | 90 | Number of days back from `end_date` to consider. | | `end_date` | str (`YYYY-MM-DD`) | `None` (defaults to today) | End of the look‑back window. | | `headers` | dict | `{}` | Include `Content-Type` or other headers if needed. | | `cookies` | dict | `{}` | Pass session or auth tokens. | | `timeout` | float | 5.0 | Seconds to wait before timing out. | | `allow_redirects` | bool | True | Follow redirects automatically. | | `verify` | bool | True | Verify SSL certificates. | --- ### Example output ```json [ { "product_id": "prod_001", "branch_id": "branch_a", "run_date": "2026-06-20T14:32:00Z", "metrics": { "accuracy": 0.987, "coverage": 0.95, "runtime_seconds": 120 } }, { "product_id": "prod_002", "branch_id": "branch_b", "run_date": "2026-06-18T09:15:00Z", "metrics": { "accuracy": 0.923, "coverage": 0.88, "runtime_seconds": 200 } } ] ``` Each entry tells you which product/branch ran, when, and how well it performed according to your defined KPIs. --- ### Quick sanity check If you want to confirm that the endpoint works without pulling all data: ```python # Get only the first 5 results response = requests_get( url="https://api.example.com/triangulation_metrics", params={"days": 7}, headers={"Accept": "application/json"}, timeout=2.0 ) print(len(response.json())) # Should print a small integer ``` That’s the gist of the **`triangulation_metrics`** function—fetch recent triangulation runs and their associated KPI snapshot.
